candidate.title: Autogenic tumor-RNA vaccine for Boxer dogs with suspected malignant glioma
candidate.center: University of Florida Small Animal Hospital
candidate.status: Currently recruiting on the official neurology index and protocol heading
candidate.intervention: Autogenic vaccine prepared from RNA extracted from the patient's glioma biopsy; three weekly vaccinations beginning two weeks after biopsy
candidate.funding: 🟡 Partially funded. Study covers CT-guided tumor biopsy and lymph-node removal, associated anesthesia/recovery, study vaccines, and research sample collection/analysis. Other visit/care costs are not itemized and must be discussed at evaluation.
candidate.contact: Neurology Staff, University of Florida Small Animal Hospital: 352-392-2235; official Study Interest Form. PI: Dr. Sheila Carrera-Justiz.
candidate.eligibility: Boxer dogs with suspected malignant glioma on a previous MRI, no other life-threatening diseases and no previous treatment for the tumor. Neurology team confirms final eligibility.
candidate.notes: The current official UF neurology index explicitly lists NOW RECRUITING and the individual protocol heading repeats it, although one background sentence uses past-tense recruited. Prior MRI evidence of suspected malignant glioma is sufficient for prescreen; biopsy occurs in the study. Boxer breed restriction is mandatory and requires investigator confirmation because the current matcher does not encode breed. Tumor biopsy is followed by three weekly vaccines starting two weeks later. Lymph-node removal follows the first vaccination; each vaccine requires at least six hours in hospital for monitoring. No previous tumor treatment is permitted. This is a distinct UF glioma protocol, not the Minnesota Zika/autologous-lysate or nanoparticle-gene protocols.
